data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Resumption is always permissible because the reasoning envelope proactively closes the event stream before budget exhaustion forces truncation, leaving no partial fragment; the only refusal condition is an implementation defect where the proactive-close mechanism fails to fire.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The proactive-close mechanism fails to fire before exhaustion, leaving a partial fragment with no clean terminal marker.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The budget monitor and the event stream share no synchronization, so exhaustion can race ahead of the close signal.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The terminal close marker itself is truncated, making it indistinguishable from a partial data record.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"If the envelope monitors remaining budget and, upon reaching a pre-exhaustion threshold, flushes all pending state into a complete terminal event and closes the stream cleanly, then no partial fragment ever exists. The append-only log contains only complete events. Resumption is simply appending new events after the terminal close marker. The problem's demand for a refusal condition is satisfied by noting the single failure mode: the proactive-close mechanism itself fails (e.g., the budget monitor crashes before triggering close). In that case the log is in an indeterminate state and resumption must be refused until an integrity scan confirms the last record is complete.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
